profile.summary: E1 (Profluent-E1) is a family of protein language models that can read a query protein sequence on its own or together with homologous sequences retrieved for it. It outputs per-residue embeddings and amino acid probabilities (logits), which are used for zero-shot fitness and variant scoring, contact map prediction and as features for structural tasks. The developers present it as a drop-in replacement for the ESM family.
profile.summary_source_locator: bioRxiv abstract; README: introduction, Interactive Usage

summary_quotes.text: we have built Profluent-E1, a family of retrieval-augmented protein language models that explicitly condition on homologous sequences
E1 can be used flexibly in single-sequence or retrieval-augmented inference mode for fitness prediction, variant ranking, and embeddings for structural tasks
They are designed to be drop-in replacement for ESM family of models.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: E1 is a masked language model (the released class is E1ForMaskedLM). In retrieval-augmented mode, homologous sequences are placed before the query, separated by commas, and the model attends across them with block-causal multi-sequence attention, so it can use family-specific evolutionary context without fine-tuning. The configuration has separate position encodings within each sequence and across the whole input, and uses global attention every third layer. The models were trained on four trillion tokens from the Profluent Protein Atlas, in BF16 precision. A `?` character marks a masked position.
sections.source_locator: bioRxiv abstract; README: Interactive Usage, Compute Requirements; config.json

quotes.text: By integrating retrieved evolutionary context through block-causal multi-sequence attention, E1 captures both general and family-specific constraints without fine-tuning.
To use the model in retrieval augmented mode, you can prepend your query with homolog sequences separated by commas.
You can use `?` as mask token.
We train E1 models on four trillion tokens from the Profluent Protein Atlas
the model was trained with BF16 precision

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three checkpoints are released: E1-150m, E1-300m and E1-600m. Hugging Face counts 154,423,330, 274,317,346 and 641,438,754 parameters in their safetensors files. E1-150m and E1-300m have 20 layers (hidden size 768 and 1024); E1-600m has 30 layers and hidden size 1280. On 2026-03-09 the developers changed the MSA sampling code to fix a bug, so results that use retrieval through the repository's sampling code should name the commit. A result should also name the checkpoint, its revision, and whether it ran in single-sequence or retrieval-augmented mode. This page read the code at commit bfd2620a.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Retrieval-augmented protein language model (masked language model and encoder) that can also run on a single sequence.

quotes.text: a family of retrieval-augmented protein language models
The model can be used in both single sequence and retrieval augmented mode.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer with block-causal multi-sequence attention over the homologs and query, separate within-sequence and global rotary position settings, global attention every 3 layers and gated MLPs. 20 layers (150m, 300m) or 30 layers (600m).

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A protein sequence, optionally preceded by homologous sequences separated by commas; `?` marks masked positions.

quotes.text: you can prepend your query with homolog sequences separated by commas

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Logits over the vocabulary and embeddings for every token; the README shows how to keep only the query's residues. Cookbooks cover zero-shot fitness, site saturation mutagenesis by masked-marginal scoring, and sequence embeddings.

run_guide.summary: Install the E1 package at a pinned commit and run E1-300m on one single sequence and one retrieval-augmented input to get logits and embeddings.
prerequisites: Python 3.12 or 3.13 (pyproject.toml), with torch between 2.7.0 and 2.9.0 and transformers below 4.57.0.
The README example runs on cuda:0. A GPU with BF16 support (CUDA capability 8.0 or higher) is recommended; GPU memory is not stated.
Downloading or using the weights binds the user to the Profluent-E1 Clickthrough License Agreement and its attribution guidelines.

steps.title: Get the code and install
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/Profluent-AI/E1.git
cd E1
git checkout --detach bfd2620a602248499f3d2583d85a7ecddf0b6e02
pip3 install -e .
steps.explanation: The README's install commands, with a checkout line added to pin the commit this page was written from.

steps.title: Optional: install flash attention
steps.explanation: Recommended by the README for GPUs with CUDA capability 8.0 or higher.

steps.title: Run the model
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch

from E1.batch_preparer import E1BatchPreparer
from E1.modeling import E1ForMaskedLM

model = E1ForMaskedLM.from_pretrained("Profluent-Bio/E1-300m").to("cuda:0")
model.eval()

sequences = ["AAAAA?C", "MFCATEEKL,MCCASDF,MFCC?SEF"]
batch_preparer = E1BatchPreparer()
batch = batch_preparer.get_batch_kwargs(sequences, device="cuda:0")

with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, enabled=True):
    outputs = model(
        input_ids=batch["input_ids"],
        within_seq_position_ids=batch["within_seq_position_ids"],
        global_position_ids=batch["global_position_ids"],
        sequence_ids=batch["sequence_ids"],
        past_key_values=None,
        use_cache=False,
        output_attentions=False,
        output_hidden_states=False,
    )

logits: torch.Tensor = outputs.logits  # (B, L, V)
embeddings: torch.Tensor = outputs.embeddings  # (B, L, E)

print(logits)
print(embeddings)
PY
steps.explanation: The first part of the README usage example, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads E1-300m and runs one single-sequence input and one input with two homologs before the query. The README continues with selectors that keep only the query's residues.

outputs: Printed logits of shape (batch, length, vocabulary) and embeddings of shape (batch, length, embedding size) for the two inputs.
